headline_marked: [[Durga Puja festivities begin]] with Maha Shasthi at 33,165 mandaps across Bangladesh
headline: Durga Puja festivities begin with Maha Shasthi at 33,165 mandaps across Bangladesh
summary: The Hindu community's largest religious festival officially starts today with the ceremonial awakening of Goddess Durga. Devotees will offer prayers for peace and prosperity.
details: Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, officially begins today in Bangladesh with Maha Shasthi. This year, the festivities will be celebrated at 33,165 mandaps across the country.

On the first day, devotees will perform Bodhan, the ceremonial awakening and invocation of Goddess Durga, marking the formal beginning of the celebrations. Devotees of all ages are expected to visit mandaps and offer prayers, seeking blessings for peace, prosperity, and welfare.

The main rituals will continue through Bijoya Dashami on October 21, concluding with the immersion of idols. Maha Saptami Puja will be observed over two days, October 17 and 18, followed by Maha Ashtami on October 19 and Maha Nabami on October 20.

Security has been significantly tightened to ensure peaceful celebrations, with members of various law enforcement agencies deployed at puja mandaps nationwide. A total of 212,118 members of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party have been deployed, with eight personnel assigned to each high-risk mandap and six to every other mandap.

An additional 104 striking teams will remain on standby to respond quickly to any untoward incident, as announced by Ansar Director General Major General Abdul Motaleb Sazzad Mahmud. Border Guard Bangladesh has also set up 18 base camps and intensified patrols near border areas to secure around 1,800 mandaps.

The government has declared a three-day holiday for Durga Puja from October 20 to 22. With October 23 and 24 falling on regular weekly holidays, the break will extend to five days, from October 20 to 24.

headline_marked: [[Most vegetables now cost over BDT 80/kg]] in Dhaka markets as winter approaches
headline: Most vegetables now cost over BDT 80/kg in Dhaka markets as winter approaches
summary: Vegetable prices have significantly increased in Dhaka markets ahead of the winter season, with most items selling for over BDT 80 per kilogram. Only papaya and pumpkin remain below this price point.
details: Ahead of the winter season, vegetable prices have surged across Dhaka markets. Most vegetables are now selling for over BDT 80 per kilogram, with only papaya and pumpkin available at lower rates.
Specific examples include cauliflower, ridge gourd, bottle gourd, taro, and pointed gourd, all priced at BDT 80 per kg. Eggplant and spiny gourd are even higher at BDT 100 per kg.
Early winter varieties like radish and okra are also BDT 80 per kg, while early winter beans are BDT 160 per kg. Tomatoes are the most expensive, ranging from BDT 180 to BDT 200 per kg.
According to vendors, prices typically rise before the full arrival of winter vegetables. An increase in truck fares, primarily due to rising fuel costs, has further impacted the prices of produce.

In contrast, broiler chicken prices have slightly decreased by BDT 5-10 per kg, now selling for BDT 175-180 per kg. Golden chicken is BDT 320-330 per kg. This drop is attributed to increased production and better supply as the summer heat subsides.

Egg prices, however, remain high and stable, with farm eggs selling for BDT 145-150 per dozen and white eggs at BDT 140 per dozen. Vendors expect prices to fall once winter vegetables become abundant.
The rice market has remained stable at last week's prices. Coarse rice is BDT 55 per kg, medium-quality Aatash or Paijam rice is BDT 55-65 per kg, and fine rice is BDT 75-80 per kg.

However, some varieties of Nazirshail rice saw a BDT 2-3 per kg increase one to one and a half weeks ago, now priced at BDT 80-86 per kg depending on quality. This increase is also linked to higher truck fares due to fuel price hikes.

Other essential items like onions are BDT 55-60 per kg, local garlic BDT 140 per kg, and imported garlic BDT 180 per kg. Chili prices are stable at BDT 100-120 per kg, and bottled soybean oil remains BDT 210 per liter.
